claim.pdf_says: Index entries printed one per line with sub-entries indented beneath their main entry, e.g. 'Nucleus, VI-1' followed by the indented sub-entry 'Element summary, I-11'
claim.markdown_says: Every entry is a bare line with no list marker, sub-entries only space-indented: 'Nucleus, VI-1' then '  Element summary, I-11'
claim.why_it_matters: Markdown renders consecutive bare lines as one paragraph, so the whole index page collapses into one run-on line and the entry boundaries and hierarchy are lost when rendered (pages 961-962 use '- ' list items). Entries and references match the PDF; informative content.

verdict.reasoning: Checked the 300 dpi render of printed page B-58 against page-970.md. The markdown keeps every entry on its own line and indents each sub-entry two spaces under its main entry, as the PDF does (NOT / EVALUATE statement VI-84 ...; Nucleus, VI-1 / Element summary, I-11; OCCURS clause / CORRESPONDING phrase VI-68 ...). The claim itself concedes that entries and page references match. The only difference is how a Markdown renderer would treat bare lines, which is presentation markup and not a content discrepancy. The task's rules exclude differences that are only formatting and do not change meaning, and this informative index page carries no normative text.
